scope: Ship verdict: develop -> main for release 0.4.7 (candidates 1-4 plus post-closure fixes), the develop tip is the merge commit of PR #253
verdict_reason: Release-level snapshot over 6cef01f854ee4e3c1178791270c9813fa9947730..e8a0242c0107b24c392d2f643ccb7f2fa2aa01cf (main's published tip .. develop's tip, the PR #253 merge commit). (a) `git diff origin/main..origin/develop --stat` -> 407 files changed, 18817(+)/11167(-); `--dirstat` confirms the surface matches the expected shape: tests/contract, tests/unit/features/specs, dadaia_workspace/features/specs, tests/integration/cli, dadaia_workspace/cli/commands, dadaia_workspace/hooks, dadaia_workspace/core, specs/memory/product, specs/releases/0.4.7 and public/skills/agents dominate -- the four candidates' known surfaces (gate policy, doctor/ledgers consolidation, release lifecycle, memory/skills work) plus chokepoint (dd-gitflow-default verdict-store two-hop rule) and doctor (backlog-doctor -> one `dadaia doctor` job) fixes visible directly in .github/workflows/ci.yml and pyproject.toml; no unexplained surface. (b) Leak grep `<home-dir>/|<home-dir>/|IPv4` over the full diff: 134 raw hits, all inspected. Every hit is one of: (i) an already-redacted `[REDACTED]` literal inside specs/bugs ledger history migrated from _archive; (ii) a documented placeholder/exclude-list form (`<home-dir>/(user|username|youruser|<user>|runner|ci|ubuntu|synthxabcd|synthxa)`, `<home-dir>/(user|...|Shared)`) that IS the denylist scanner's own pattern definition, not a leak; (iii) synthetic test fixtures (`<home-dir>/operator`, `<home-dir>/testuser`, `<home-dir>/op`, `test-session-*` telemetry fixtures) that are the product's own test data; (iv) IPv4 hits that are either the loopback address (loopback, intentional -- panel binds loopback-only per project memory), RFC5737 TEST-NET literals (a TEST-NET literal) replacing RFC1918 literals (two RFC1918 literals) in test fixtures -- a REMEDIATION, not a regression -- or version strings (`0.4.x`) misf-matched by the digit-group regex. One noteworthy hit (tests/unit/test_backlog_models.py, a `-`/`+` pair): the diff REMOVES the literal operator username path `<home-dir>/workspace/foo.py#Bar` (a pre-existing, already-published-on-main negative-test fixture demonstrating 'an absolute operator-local path must never bind as a code ref') and replaces it with the generic placeholder `<home-dir>/user/workspace/foo.py#Bar` -- this is a remediation of a pre-existing minor privacy smell already on main's history, not a new introduction; the value never leaves the diff as a live path (it names this operator's own workstation, already a matter of published git history predating this release, not newly disclosed by this range). Zero net-new unredacted absolute path, IP, or hostname. (c) `git grep -n -i -E '<sibling-family>' origin/develop -- . ':!specs/bugs/_archive' ':!specs/releases/_archive'` -> 0 hits (the sibling family name is fully absent from the develop tree outside the excluded archive paths -- exceeds the carve-out, nothing to disposition). Secret-pattern grep `(password|passwd|secret|token|api_key|apikey|private_key)\s*=\s*["'][^"']{6,}` over the full diff -> 1 raw hit, a `-` (removed) line: `secret = "<secret-token>"` in a chokepoint denylist-scan test, AWS's own documented non-functional EXAMPLE key literal, and the diff replaces it with a runtime-composed `aws_key_shape()` helper -- matches DADAIA.md 7.4 ('a fixture needing a secret shape composes it at runtime, never as a tracked literal') exactly; a remediation, not a finding. `BEGIN.*PRIVATE KEY` grep over the full diff -> 2 raw hits, both inside verdict-prose (the superseded 00497199/448d365e handoff text) quoting the grep PATTERN itself as part of a prior scan's own description -- no private-key material, confirmed by direct read. (d) Dependency/lockfile/CI: `git diff --stat -- pyproject.toml poetry.lock .github` -> poetry.lock untouched (0 dependency version changes in range); pyproject.toml gains `[tool.ruff] cache-dir` and `[tool.mypy] cache_dir` (both relative paths under `../../.dadaia/tmp/`, redirecting caches outside the repo tree per DADAIA.md 5.3 -- no absolute path, no new credential surface), a `[tool.poetry.urls]` block (public PyPI/GitHub URLs only, no secret), and version 0.4.6 -> 0.4.7; .github/workflows/ci.yml drops the blanket `fetch-depth: 0` from every checkout step (reduces exposure of full git history to CI runners -- a hardening, not a weakening) and consolidates the `backlog-doctor` job into one `dadaia doctor` job (functional rename, same invariants: BL-SCHEMA/CONFLICT/STALE plus SPEC-DOC/RELEASE-TREE, still fails the job on any error-class finding); no IaC file (Dockerfile/compose/Terraform/Pulumi) touched anywhere in the range. `pip-audit` on the dev venv: 47 known findings across 5 packages (dulwich 0.21.7, msgpack 1.1.2, pillow 12.2.0, pip 24.0, poetry 1.8.3) -- all pre-existing dev-tooling CVEs unrelated to this release's diff (poetry.lock unchanged, confirming these versions are not newly introduced), not a production dependency (the two project packages dadaia-workspace/dm-capture-utils are correctly unaudited, not on PyPI) -- carried forward as a known, non-blocking open item, not new to 0.4.7. (e) Prior verdict chain, each covering a sub-range of this same 6cef01f8..e8a0242c span, all APPROVED, 0 findings at time of issuance: e214a463 (candidate 4 PR-gate), 62369eb9 (candidates 2-4 PR-gate), 448d365e (delta re-verdict), 00497199 (delta re-verdict, superseded by this session's PR-gate verdict alongside this ship verdict) -- each individually reviewed its slice of the range with the same method (OWASP scan, secret grep, leak grep, dependency check); this ship verdict is the release-level snapshot re-confirming the union of those slices plus the small residual (CI/pyproject hardening, test-fixture remediations) visible only in the full main..develop diff and not in any single candidate's delta. No CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM finding. No production dependency version changed. No IaC surface touched. No live credential, no PII, no auth/access-control regression identified anywhere in the range. Snapshot, not a guarantee of 'secure' (DADAIA.md 7.5) -- the operator owns the ship decision.
